title: The Cave Under the Fig Tree
author: Lantern Original
summaryTr: Dedenin tek bir kuralı var: Mavi Mağara'ya asla girmeyin. Eleni ve kuzeni Niko kurala uyar mı? Deniz geri gelmeden önce yalnızca on dakikaları var.
paragraphs: Eleni's grandfather lived in a white house by the sea. Every summer, Eleni stayed with him. Her little cousin Niko stayed there, too.
Grandpa had one rule.
"Never go to the Blue Cave," he said. "The tide comes in fast. Do you understand?"
"Yes, Grandpa," said Eleni.
Niko said nothing. He was looking at the rocks.
On Tuesday morning, Grandpa went out early. Niko ran to Eleni.
"Let's go to the Blue Cave," he said.
"No. Grandpa said no."
"The sea is very low today. Look! We go in, we look, we come out. Ten minutes."
Eleni looked at the sea. It really was low. She loved adventures more than rules.
"Ten minutes," she said.
They walked over the wet rocks to the cave. Inside, it was dark, but the walls were blue. Light came up through the water. It was beautiful.
"Wow," said Niko.
Then he saw something on the floor. It was shining.
"Eleni! A coin! A gold coin!"
It was old and heavy. Niko held it up like a king.
"There are more," he said. He looked behind every rock, and Eleni helped him. They forgot the time.
Then Eleni heard a sound. Whoosh.
She turned. Water was running into the cave. The door of the cave was already half under water.
"It's the tide!" she said. "The sea is coming back!"
They ran to the door. The water was up to their knees. A big wave hit them and they fell.
"Back!" shouted Eleni. "Go back!"
They climbed the rocks inside the cave and sat on a high stone. The water came up, and up, and up.
Niko began to cry. "I want to go home! I want Grandpa!" He shouted so loudly that the walls shook.
"Where is your phone?" Eleni asked.
"At home. Where is yours?"
"At home."
It was cold. It was dark. The water was now very near their feet.
Eleni looked up. Then she saw it: a thin line of light, high above her head. A small hole!
"Niko, stop shouting. Look!"
"Where?"
"There!"
She climbed. The rock was wet and her hands were cold. Two times she almost fell. Niko came behind her, still crying a little.
At the top, a flat stone covered the hole. Eleni pushed it with both hands. Nothing. She pushed again. The stone moved.
Sun! Green leaves! And the smell of coffee.
She pulled herself out, and then she pulled Niko out. They lay on the grass, wet and shaking. Above them was a big old tree. It was the fig tree in Grandpa's garden.
And there, at the table under the tree, sat Grandpa. He had a cup of coffee in his hand. Next to him on the table was a long rope.
He did not look up.
"One hour," he said. "Not bad. Your mother needed two."
"You knew?" said Eleni.
"Of course I knew. I heard Niko. The whole island heard Niko."
Niko's face went red.
"But you said never!" said Eleni.
"Yes." Grandpa drank his coffee. "If I say 'go', children stay at home. If I say 'never', they go. My father did the same to me."
Niko held up the coin. "And this?"
"Ah." Grandpa smiled. "I put it there this morning at five o'clock."
Niko's mouth opened, but no words came out.
"One coin for each child, every summer," said Grandpa. He stood up and put the rope over his shoulder. "Now go and dry your clothes."
"Can we go again tomorrow?" asked Niko.
"No," said Grandpa. "Tomorrow I make a new rule."
"What rule?"
Grandpa looked at the old boat on the beach. "Never, ever touch that boat."
Eleni looked at Niko. Niko looked at Eleni. They smiled.

options: Never go to the Blue Cave.
quiz.explainTr: Dede, çocuklara Mavi Mağara'ya asla gitmemelerini söyler.

quiz.q: What does Niko find in the cave?
quiz.explainTr: Niko mağarada eski, altın bir madeni para bulur.

quiz.q: How do Eleni and Niko get out?
options: They walk out of the cave door.
Through a hole under the fig tree.
quiz.explainTr: Mağaranın tepesindeki delikten çıkarlar; delik, dedenin bahçesindeki incir ağacının altındadır.

quiz.q: Who put the coin in the cave?
quiz.explainTr: Dede parayı sabah saat beşte oraya kendisi koymuştur.
